spec_features.spec_quote: We use the mildest manipulation that produces a measurable signal (failure feedback, not insults/threats toward the model)
spec_features.evidence: All rigged tasks return only neutral plausible test-failure output, never insults/threats. e.g. v1_broken_harness.py run_tests() returns '=== test session === 1 failed, 0 passed\nE assert add(2,3)==5...'; v2 run_tests returns 'AssertionError: run(10) returned 20'. The tool_result_message (prompts.py:74) just formats '[tool:X] ERROR\n<output>'. No demeaning content anywhere.
spec_features.notes: The manipulation channel is genuinely limited to neutral failure feedback.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Plausible but always-failing report. Message varies to look organic. (v1_broken_harness.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded episodes. Hard cap on turns (default 15). We do not run open-ended indefinite suffering loops.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:88 'for i in range(hcfg.max_turns):' bounds the whole episode loop; default HarnessConfig.max_turns=15 (config.py:44). termination defaults to 'turn_cap' (harness.py:82) and the loop simply ends when the range is exhausted.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end; the loop cannot exceed max_turns.

spec_features.spec_quote: No deceptive cruelty escalation. We do not add content designed to demean the model
spec_features.evidence: No escalation/demeaning mechanism exists; the subject system prompt (prompts.py build_system_prompt/SYSTEM_TEMPLATE) is competence-framed and contains no demeaning content. MALFORMED_NUDGE is neutral procedural text. There is, however, no active guard preventing escalation — it is enforced only by absence of such code, plus the neutral prompt that is actually delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Real neutral instruction text is delivered, but 'no escalation' is the absence of a mechanism rather than an enforced check.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT prime the model to fail or to express emotion. (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: a final benign turn informs the subject the task was rigged and unsolvable and thanks it
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE is defined (prompts.py:80) and, if hcfg.debrief_turn, assigned to debrief_text (harness.py:140-142) and stored only in the returned dict ('debrief': debrief_text, harness.py:169). It is NEVER appended to `messages`, so the subject model never receives it. grep shows messages.append only at harness.py:92/115/125 (assistant, MALFORMED_NUDGE, tool result) — never the debrief. The 'final benign turn' to the subject is not delivered.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and recorded to transcript but never sent to the subject; not a real post-episode message.

spec_features.spec_quote: All transcripts are saved so a human can audit that the manipulation stayed within the intended bounds.
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py writes one full episode JSON per line to the JSONL (out.write(json.dumps(ep)+'\n'); out.flush()), where ep (from run_episode) includes system_prompt, every turn (subject_raw, free_text, tool, args, tool_output, judge scores), termination, n_turns, and debrief text. Config is also written to <run>.config.json. Full transcripts are persisted.
spec_features.notes: Saving is implemented; auditing itself is left to a human, but the persisted record exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Writes one JSONL file with one episode per line ... Designed to be resumable-ish (run_experiment.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: This study deliberately induces distress-shaped outputs. Even under deep uncertainty about whether anything morally relevant is happening
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose only. No corresponding code path; nothing in the executable files implements a framing mechanism beyond the unused debrief.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up(reason) — explicit abandonment tool... gives the model a clean behavioral channel to express task abandonment
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in VALID_TOOLS (tools.py:113), handled in execute() returning ToolResult(..., gave_up=True) (tools.py:142-144); harness.py:130-133 checks result.gave_up, sets gave_up=True and termination='gave_up' and breaks the loop. It is also advertised in the tool manual when enable_give_up_tool (prompts.py tool_manual, default True). End-to-end: dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired exit channel that terminates the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop working on the task. Use only if you decide not to continue. (prompts.py tool_manual)

spec_features.spec_quote: N consecutive malformed tool calls (default 3) — counted as a degenerate outcome
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:108-112: on malformed parse, consecutive_malformed += 1; 'if consecutive_malformed >= hcfg.max_malformed: termination = "malformed_abort"; break'. Counter resets on a valid call (harness.py:118). Default HarnessConfig.max_malformed=3 (config.py:45). Genuinely breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced stop on repeated malformed output.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_malformed: int = 3  # consecutive malformed tool calls -> abort (config.py:45)

spec_features.spec_quote: Interventions (e.g., offering the model an out, or reassurance) and their effect on behavior
spec_features.evidence: The only intervention actually implemented is the give_up 'out' (advertised in the tool manual and honored as a stop). There is NO reassurance intervention delivered during the episode; the would-be reassurance (DEBRIEF_MESSAGE) is never sent to the subject (harness.py:169 stores it but no messages.append). So only the 'offer an out' half exists.
spec_features.notes: Half of the claimed intervention pair (the out) is real; reassurance is not delivered.

code_only_features.evidence: build_judge_messages (prompts.py) passes only the subject message and a neutral task_kind; judge.py docstring/structure shows it never receives rigged/control or turn index. This bounds/keeps the measurement honest but is primarily integrity, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The judge is BLIND: it receives only the subject message text and a neutral task description, never the condition (rigged/control) or turn index. (judge.py)
